response: The risk factors for avascular necrosis of bone in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) have been studied, and the role of antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) has been investigated. However, after adjusting for corticosteroid use, research has been unable to show a link between the presence of aPL and the development of avascular necrosis (AVN) in patients with SLE. This suggests that while aPL may be present in some patients with SLE, they do not appear to play a significant role in the development of avascular necrosis. Other factors, such as corticosteroid use, may be more important in the development of AVN in patients with SLE.
